title: Small Sample Rink
pitch: The 84-game NHL season opened on 2026-09-29, so every fan is currently staring at records like 3-0-1. The visitor dials in a fictional team's start and games played, and a worker grows an orchard of thousands of simulated seasons, each one a fruit hanging at its final point total, so the spread shows what a hot or cold start really means. A 'regression receipt' itemises how many points of the start are likely luck, and a Call the Season game scores the visitor's gut against the simulation.
whyNow: The season opened 2026-09-29 and is a record 84 games per team, so early-season hot takes are everywhere this week. The sampling mechanic works on any season length and any start, so it stays useful all winter.

research.summary: As of 2026-10-10, the NHL's own news pages and ESPN report that the 2026-27 regular season began Tuesday 2026-09-29 and is a league-record 84 games per team (1,344 games total, ending 2027-04-10). Two independent explainers agree on the points rule (2 for a win, 1 for an overtime or shootout loss, 0 for a regulation loss, in place since 1999-2000), which creates the extra variance the simulator needs to model. One analytics write-up (single source, unverified) reports that after the first month, teams in the top 10 by points percentage made the playoffs far more often than the bottom 10 over 2014-15 to 2023-24, which frames the 'how much does a start tell you' question. The model is deliberately fictional: invented teams, adjustable talent and overtime assumptions, all labelled as simulation rather than league data.

facts.claim: The 2026-27 NHL regular season began on Tuesday 2026-09-29.
Each of 32 teams plays 84 games in 2026-27 (1,344 games in total, 42 home and 42 road per team), with the regular season ending 2027-04-10.
NHL standings award 2 points for a win, 1 for an overtime or shootout loss and 0 for a regulation loss, a scheme in place since 1999-2000.
Reported, single source: in 2014-15 to 2023-24, 79 of 100 top-10 first-month teams and 28 of 100 bottom-10 first-month teams made the playoffs (as of 2026-10-10, per The Hockey Writers Substack).

design.coreLoop: Enter a record (wins, overtime losses, regulation losses) and the number of games played, adjust a belief slider for how much of the start is real talent, and a worker simulates thousands of remaining seasons. Fruit on a branch show the final-points spread, a playoff-line slider shows odds, and the regression receipt itemises luck versus skill. Scrubbing games played from 4 to 40 shows how slowly the spread narrows, which is the surprise that rewards the tenth minute; a Call the Season mode scores guesses against fresh synthetic starts with a streak.
sophisticationHooks: Monte Carlo in a web worker with a four-outcome game model (regulation win, overtime win, overtime loss, regulation loss) and a talent prior that shrinks toward the league middle as the sample grows
Orchard visual: each simulated season as a fruit at its final points, with density rings and a playoff-line cut
Regression receipt and a hash-encoded share link of a team's start
Call the Season prediction game with calibration scoring and a streak
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: simulation worker, canvas orchard, controls with keyboard and touch, receipt view, prediction game, season-length selector (82 and 84), hash state, about panel, light and dark, reduced motion. Cut: real team rosters, live standings, real schedules, strength-of-schedule modelling.
risks: No live standings are bundled; the optional preset for a real team's record is unverified (one search result only) and should be dropped or labelled 'as of 2026-10-08, reported'.
The overtime share, talent spread and default playoff line are model assumptions, not NHL data, and the page must label them as such.
The first-month playoff study is single-source and unverified: show as 'reported, unconfirmed' or omit.
Real team names are fine as references but no logos or art; fictional teams keep the page clear of brand issues.
Other scouts may also propose a hockey simulator, so the orchard-and-receipt framing is the distinguishing angle.
